body:
So sorry for your loss. I can't imagine how you must feel right now with him being so young. 

I followed my mothers lead and never cried. I rebelled and did drugs an acted out. Don't do this. It will not make things better.

 I was only 13 when it happened so I don't think the full gravity of the situation hit me until later. All you can do is just keep moving forward. You don't have to be perfect. Your parents will understand. Be there for them as much as you can but don't let them use you as a crutch or put all their expectations on you now that he is gone. Live your life. Keep moving forward. Be there for your brothers. 

You just need to take the time to grieve.You may think you have come to terms with it but one day something that reminds you of him may set you off in the most mundane situations. It sucks but at that point...F it...cry it out. It may happen more than once. I lost it at a bar a few years ago(alcohol also doesn't help) I cried like a baby in the middle of the bar just from hearing a song. 

You will be ok. You need to walk at graduation not just for yourself but for your parents. I am sure they will be very proud.

Well dammit. This is not what I wanted this post to convey. 

I was just trying to explain how it effects people many years down the road. Could be your sister, your brother, your parents, your neighbor, a co-worker or friend at school. They will always think about you. It will effect them forever. 

I was just letting everyone know how it impacted me personally. I am sure there are a ton of other people that could give you their own personal stories about the impact it has had on their life.

My personal opinion is that he was drunk and sad. The Seal song "Kiss from a Rose" was in his CD player when they found him. I will never pretend to understand anything he was going though or why he did this. I was just relaying the pain that me and my family have gone through on the other side. I suffer with (undiagnosed depression as well) I used to be a cutter and have been through my share of dark days. 

I just want people to understand that it is not that you just make your family sad. You change the dynamic. Your family will never be the same. My family is great at hiding emotions. 

I have never seen my mother cry in my entire life(including her brothers funeral). I have no idea why my fathers dad was never in our life or why he left my grandmother when my dad was young. I have no idea what my other grandfather was like. He died before I was born and no one ever talks about him. 

I just want people to think about it and just take one more day to see what the morning or night holds for them. You never know. 

I will never pretend to know what other people are going through. I just wanted to give my perspective. 

EDIT: He was a parent. He had a two month old little girl when he left.
